Subject: Unexpected duplicate charges across July invoices

Jonas —

We're seeing an unusual set of charges across two July invoices (inv# 2025-07-0012 and inv# 2025-07-0034). The total tokens billed look like they're approximately 2.1x our expected consumption for that period. Our engineering team noticed a pattern where session ids seem duplicated across two different API keys. Can you help us understand how Redwood attributes token counts to invoices when multiple keys are used from the same customer org?

We need a short explanation and any preliminary evidence so we can hold payment on the second invoice while we investigate internally. We can share logs if that helps.

Thanks,

Hi Anna — thanks for flagging and sharing the sample attachment. I'm looping in Lauren from Finance and Marissa from CS so we can triage quickly.

Short answer up-front: Redwood attributes usage to the API key and tenant tagging at ingest time. If the same session-level activity is routed via two keys (or if a client switched keys mid-session without a stable session identifier), we can end up with two attribution records that look like duplicates. That can show up as extra tokens on a later invoice depending on ingestion windows and invoice cutoffs.

Next steps:
- Lauren, can you pull the ledger rows for the two invoice IDs Anna mentioned and look for overlapping session identifiers or identical request_hash values?
- Marissa, can CS confirm whether we have a session-stitching/fingerprint rule in place for BrightGrid (they're on a hybrid ingest path).

Anna — if you can send 2–3 more sample request ids from July (or grant access to the Drive link you mentioned), that'll speed root cause. We can provisionally place a hold on inv# 2025-07-0034 while we investigate if you'd like.

—Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — I've pulled the ledger for inv# 2025-07-0012 and 2025-07-0034. Preliminary findings attached: billing_sample_202507.json contains the token-level rows we attribute to BrightGrid's tenant id and the API keys in use.

What I see: there are ~1.9M tokens in rows tied to request_hashes that also appear in the later invoice's time window. The pattern is consistent with duplicate ingestion — same request_hash, two attribution keys.

Questions for Anna:
1) Can you confirm whether BrightGrid rotated keys in July or were running two services with separate keys?
2) If you can share 3 full request ids (the long GUID in the logs) we can match them exactly and, if duplicates are confirmed, propose a retroactive credit.

Proposal: if we confirm duplication for >50% of the disputed tokens, Redwood will issue a credit to offset the duplicated portion and place the later invoice on hold until reconciliation completes.

Thanks Lauren — we did a quick check on our side and found that two backend services (ingest-svc and realtime-proxy) were both sending the same session payload during a partial migration. We rotated a key on 2025-07-14 but didn't fully stop the old service until 2025-07-20, which explains the overlap.

I've dropped three sample request ids in the Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b3cBillingSample. The sample lines include the request_guid and timestamp.

We appreciate the provisional hold on inv# 2025-07-0034 while you confirm. Let us know what evidence you need to move forward with a credit.

—Anna
BrightGrid

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate charges across July invoices — proposed resolution

Anna — quick update and proposed next steps:

1) Finance matched the three sample request GUIDs you provided to ledger rows; each GUID appears twice under different api_key values (ingest-svc key and proxy key). We identified ~1.05M duplicated prompt+completion tokens attributable to the overlap window 2025-07-14T00:00:00Z through 2025-07-20T23:59:59Z.

2) Proposed remediation: issue a credit equal to the duplicated tokens (1.05M tokens) at the prevailing rate on the invoice and apply the credit to inv# 2025-07-0034. We'll place that invoice on hold until the credit posts.

3) Technical recommendation: implement a short-lived request_fingerprint header or stable session id on your clients; alternatively enable "prefix-tagging" on the client side so multiple keys do not create separate attribution for the same session. Marissa will follow up with an implementation note and a CS checklist.

If you confirm the credit amount and approve the hold, we'll start the billing adjustment and send an updated invoice.

Thanks for working through this — sorry for the disruption.

—Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
